alternatives.label: Business strategy, markets and organisational decisions
alternatives.concept: Studies business decisions through entrepreneurship, accounting, finance, economics, strategy, marketing, organisational psychology, negotiation and business law. Research and data methods support analysis; programming and AI provide context for changing firms. Supply-chain operations, advanced accounting and the dedicated VU specialisation thesis remain gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme spans the functional areas of business and emphasises strategy, markets and organisational decisions without claiming to be solely a finance or marketing major.

alternatives.label: Digital business, AI and new ventures
alternatives.concept: Studies new ventures and digital change through business foundations, strategy, marketing and organisational study alongside programming, databases, algorithms, machine learning and neural networks. The technical courses provide computational methods rather than a guaranteed business application in every project. AI ethics and responsible transformation connect these tools with management questions.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set includes entrepreneurship and marketing alongside several computing and AI courses, which materially define this programme.

alternatives.label: People, leadership and organisational change
alternatives.concept: Studies business organisations through leadership, communication, diversity, organisational psychology, social influence and change. Accounting, economics, strategy, marketing and law retain a business foundation; qualitative and multivariate methods support investigation. The focus is people and organisations rather than a full strategic-HRM or supply-chain qualification.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed course set puts leadership, organisational behaviour and research into employee and team processes at its centre.

routeSelection.route: Strategy and Organisation (Strategie en Organisatie) specialisation
routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized Bedrijfskunde target requires one of the formally listed year-three specialisations to be instantiated. Strategy and Organisation is the broadest management/organisational strategy direction rather than a narrow functional area; the two named 6-EC units and linked 12-EC thesis are taken together from annex VII of the adopted 2026–27 OER. This academic representation was chosen before comparing UCR courses.

notes.text: These UCR programmes provide substantive related business study, with different emphases on strategy, digital ventures or people and organisational change. They do not reproduce VU’s supply-chain sequence, advanced accounting choice or dedicated specialisation thesis. Optional independent research is separate, requires approval and is outside the displayed 24-course, 180-EC schedules; it does not replace the VU thesis. A curriculum comparison does not establish degree equivalence, professional qualification or automatic master’s admission.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Business Administration studies organisations through strategy, marketing, accounting, finance, people, law, logistics and information technology. The selected Strategy and Organisation route combines these foundations with research methods, a specialisation and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three substantive related programmes: broad business strategy and decisions; digital business and new ventures; and people, leadership and organisational change. Their business courses are supported by different analytical tools. Computational courses teach general methods rather than guaranteed business applications. Supply-chain depth, advanced accounting and the dedicated VU specialisation thesis remain important differences.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 60 EC in year one, 48 EC of required second-year study and two 6 EC restricted choices, then 30 EC of open academic choice, 6 EC ethics, 12 EC specialisation courses and a 12 EC individual thesis. Accounting II and Entrepreneurship are selected choices rather than requirements for every student. Noncredit research participation gates the integration-course credits. The entry language assessment and any required remediation are part of Academic Skills; personal and professional development also carries no extra credits. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 48 EC. Minor entry, level, overlap and approval rules apply. Thesis entry requires completion of years one and two, with strict methods requirements and separate course/supervisor registration.
